title: Coordinated Live Unfreeze & Patchback Play for Cross-Environment Model Rollout Regressions
creator: Aisha Kaplan
description:
Summary:
We saw a progressive canary degradation affecting a small cohort of Dedicated and Private tenants after model v2026-03-12c rollout. Symptoms: elevated token latency, increased retry rate, and incoherent completions for structured-output routes. Initial mitigation (pinned fallback model) reduced error rate but did not clear KV-cache-induced hallucinations for affected slices. This ticket codifies a live 'Unfreeze & Patchback' play: coordinated KV-resync, temporary unfreeze of canary routing, and hotpatch rollforward to a compat-quantized variant across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with explicit customer communication and rollback handshake.

Why this is different / goal:
- Address regressions that persist despite variant fallback because of stale KV/prefix cache or interrupted KV migration during rollout.
- Provide a minimal blast-radius remediation that restores acceptable quality quickly while preserving tenant isolation and auditability.
- Define a customer-facing communication template and tranche-based operational checklist to avoid repeated escalations.

Scope / Impacted surfaces:
- Serving runtime: KV cache resync, prefix-cache invalidation, model variant pinning
- Routing & control plane: staged unfreeze of canary gates, reroute policies for Dedicated pools
- Private/VPC upgrades: remote patch handshake with on-prem agent (requires field ops)
- Observability: per-tenant latency/quality dashboards, synthetic evals for key prompt families

Runbook (ordered):
1) Triage & Safety: declare Incident-Canary (pager/Slack incident channel), confirm customer-affecting tenants via console slice map. Notify CSMs for high-paying tenants.
2) Short-term Isolation: enable per-route circuit-breaker to divert new traffic to fallback variant (compat-1.18-small). Keep existing in-flight requests draining for 60s.
3) KV Inspection: run kv-check across affected host shards (tools/kvtool kv-check --slice $SLICE) and capture top-keys exhibiting high misses. Create dataset for synthetic replay.
4) Prefix flush / resync: perform targeted prefix flush for affected slices (admin flush-prefix --tenant $TENANT --prefix-checksum $SUM). Coordinate with Dedicated infra to avoid cross-tenant cache clearing.
5) Unfreeze handshake: temporarily open canary gate to allow controlled replay traffic from synthetic harness only. Verify that resynced prefixes produce stable generations under canary policy.
6) Patchback rollout: deploy hotpatch (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1543) that contains 1) KV reconciliation safety checks, 2) fallback-variant traffic splitter, and 3) instrumentation for stale-kv metrics. Roll forward to 10% of affected slices, monitor for 15m, then expand.
7) Customer comms & rollback decision: if synthetic and production traces show quality recovery within 30m, proceed; otherwise initiate negotiated rollback to previous pinned model and run KV rehydration job.
8) Post-incident follow-up: create RCA, update routing policies and add synthetic prompt coverage for observed failure modes.

Commands / artifacts (links):
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/incident-623451
- KV tooling PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1539 (kv-check additions)
- Hotpatch PR (patchback): https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1543
- Synthetic harness: gs://redwood-evals/2026-03/canary-unfreeze-replays.tar.gz
- Customer comms draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Uunfreeze-623451 (internal)

Acceptance criteria (what "done" looks like):
- Affected tenants restored to pre-rollout quality (SLOs within 10% of baseline for latency and quality-metric) as seen in per-tenant dashboards.
- KV stale-miss metric reduced to baseline for the slices in question.
- All hotpatch changes merged, release note added, & rollout policy updated to include KV preflight checks.
- Customer-facing message reviewed by Support and Sent for impacted accounts.

Trade-offs & risks considered:
- Aggressive prefix flush can cause cold-cache latency spike; mitigated by tranche-based flush and traffic shaping.
- Immediate full rollback reduces risk fast but loses opportunity to validate patchback; chosen compromise: 30m observation window during staggered patchback.
- Private deployments require field ops sign-off; increases time-to-remediate for on-prem customers — include clear SLA in comms.

Progress updates / timeline:
- 2026-03-14 09:12 UTC: Alert from synthetic monitors triggered (Marco).
- 2026-03-14 09:26 UTC: Declared Incident-Canary, notified CSMs for top-5 tenants (Aisha).
- 2026-03-14 10:03 UTC: Short-term isolation applied; fallback variant pinned to compat-1.18-small (Marco). Error rate dropped 40% but hallucination errors persisted for tenants A, C.
- 2026-03-14 11:00 UTC: KV inspection run; found high prefix-miss rate on shard-7 with partial migration marker (kv-migration-in-progress flag).
- 2026-03-14 12:10 UTC: Hotpatch PR 1543 created; includes telemetry and safe-resync step; request review from runtime leads (Riley Chen, Priya Singh).
- 2026-03-14 14:40 UTC: Staggered unfreeze to synthetic traffic only; observed stable quality on replay after prefix flush (Marco).
- 2026-03-15 02:20 UTC: Expanded patchback to 30% affected slices; monitoring green for 45m.

Reviews / feedback: 
- Priya Singh: asked to add additional guardrail that fails open if KV reconciliation takes >5m to avoid blocking traffic. Action: added timeout to hotpatch (done).
- Riley Chen: requested clearer metrics for human decision point; added a composite "customer-quality-index" (CQI) to dashboard.
- Support (Leah Ortiz): requested standardized customer message with expected timeline and rollback clause; draft updated and approved.

Follow-ups & long-term work items (separate tickets recommended):
- Add KV preflight checks to rollout pipeline (PM ticket).
- Expand synthetic prompt suite to cover structured-output routes that tripped (ENG-NEW-KV-EVAL).
- Automate tranche-based prefix flush with safe cooling period (ENG-654210).

Notes for on-call and field engineers:
- When contacting on-prem field ops, include the exact artifact: hotpatch container sha (sha256:4ac8c9...) and the signed patch manifest.
- Use internal tool for tenant slice mapping: console->slices->filter by model-version.
- If rollback is initiated for Private deployments, coordinate maintenance window with customer and capture consent via support ticket before proceeding.

Decision log:
- 2026-03-14 10:45 UTC: Decision to attempt patchback + prefix flush rather than immediate global rollback (Aisha, Marco, Priya). Rationale: targeted measures reduce customer-facing downtime while allowing us to validate fix for stale-KV root cause.

Required approvals to close this ticket:
- Runtime engineering tech lead (Riley Chen) - code and rollout approval
- Support lead (Leah Ortiz) - customer communications verified
- Field Ops lead (Diego Morales) - private deployment patch handshake verified

Closing checklist:
- [ ] Merge PR 1543 and tag release for runtime-1.22.1
- [ ] Publish post-incident RCA and update rollout runbooks
- [ ] Send final customer update and log consent for any Private rollbacks
- [ ] Create follow-up tickets for automation and synthetic coverage

Historical context: similar incidents in the last 12 months were often caused by interrupted KV migrations and asymmetric cache invalidations during mixed-topology rollouts. This play synthesizes lessons from ENG-524681 and ENG-47209 and formalizes a safer tranche-based approach with stronger customer comms.
